MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
September 3, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on Tuesday,
September 3, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Traina led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Public Works Director Damasse,
Community Services Director McPherron, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Traina seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

3.  PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Estrada presented a certificate of recognition to Steven Robles, Lomita resident, for his
extraordinary achievement of swimming from Catalina Island to Rancho Palos Verdes for a
charitable cause. Mr. Robles described his experience of swimming from Catalina Island to
Rancho Palos Verdes, and stated that proceeds from his fundraising efforts would go to help an
orphanage in Nicaragua.

4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance that staff would continue monitoring Senate
Bill 594, regarding a proposed law prohibiting the use of public funds for campaign activities,
and if the bill is still on the Senate floor with opposition from the League of California Cities
come September 16, 2013, then staff will bring forward a resolution opposing the bill.

City Manager Rock reported that along with himself, Councilmembers Sanchez and Gazeley
met Maxine Waters, U.S. Congresswoman, to discuss the idea of a Community Center in
Lomita, CDBG funding, and the possibility of obtaining a long-term lease for the baseball field
from the Navy. According to City Manager Rock, CDBG funding over the years has been
significantly reduced to the point where the City cannot initiate any new projects, however, City

  Page 1
 Manager Rock did state that there is a possibility of purchasing unused CDBG funding from
other cities.

Councilmember Gazeley complimented City Manager Rock for being very knowledgeable about
City issues and projects, and for his professionalism during their meeting with U.S.
Congresswoman Maxine Waters.

5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Cindy Segawa, Lomita resident, stated that remarks made by one of the Councilmembers to
Lomita residents was upsetting to her, and she hoped that those remarks were not true.

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, asked City Council to consider placing an item on a future
agenda to discuss e-cigarette businesses and the possibility of establishing regulations for those
types of businesses in Lomita. Furthermore, Mr. McGrath stated that some commercial
businesses in Lomita, foremost being some medical offices, do not have proper handicap
access; he asked staff to address the issue.

James Thompson, Executive Board Member of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, thanked
Mayor Estrada, Councilmember Gazeley, and City staff for attending the Coffee with the
Chamber event in City Hall, and he noted that the event was very well attended. Mr. Thompson
also invited those in attendance to the Chamber’s next Business Networking Mixer, which will
take place at the Railroad Museum on Thursday, September 26, 2013, from 5:30 p.m. to 7:30
p.m.

Marty Spain, Lomita resident, concurred with Ms. Segawa that some negative comments had
been made by one of the Councilmembers to Lomita resident. Mr. Spain also questioned
allocations from the Water Fund to City Council and the City Attorney, and asked what the
justification was for such allocations. Furthermore, Mr. Spain stated that he was opposed to
water blending in Lomita.

George Kivett, Lomita resident and Representative of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce,
strongly suggested that City Council consider having the City participate in the upcoming
International Council of Shopping Centers’ Western Division Conference, which Mr. Kivett stated
would benefit the City by potentially bringing more businesses to the area. Mr. Kivett also stated
that he was concerned with public safety in Lomita, as he recently observed a grab-and-run
incident, as well as someone posing as a salesperson at his residence.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Sanchez stated that he wanted to clarify some information regarding water
quality in Lomita, as some misinformation has been circulated in the community. According to
Councilmember Sanchez, the amounts of polyphosphates in the water are at a level of 4.5 mm,
which is less than that in the food we eat every day, and that some of the foods we eat have
polyphosphate counts as high as 10 mm. Councilmember Sanchez also stated that chromium
is non-detectable and not present in Lomita water.

Councilmember Sanchez requested a future agenda item in order to revisit the requirements of
the Congestion Management Plan (CMP), which was approved during the City Council Meeting

  Page 2
 on August 19, 2013. According to Councilmember Sanchez, Caltrans could assist with obtaining
the traffic counts at the two major intersections, which in turn would bring the City of Lomita in
compliance with the requirements of the CMP. Councilmembers Gazeley and Traina agreed to
place the agenda item request on a future agenda.

Councilmember Sanchez requested a future agenda item to appeal the Planning Commission’s
decision regarding the approval of Conditional Use Permit #281, which was approved on August
12, 2013, in accordance with the Lomita Municipal Code Section 11-1.70.16, which provides that
City Council can initiate an appeal of any action of the Planning Commission within 30 days.
According to Councilmember Sanchez, on August 12, 2013, the Planning Commission
conditionally approved a request to permit an eight unit, mixed-use development with 2,900
square feet of commercial space, located at 25114-8 Narbonne Avenue, in the C-G (Commercial
General) Zone; Councilmember Sanchez stated that he had concerns regarding parking spaces
and the proposed reduction in commercial floor area. Councilmembers Gazeley and Traina
agreed with Councilmember Sanchez to direct staff to take the necessary actions to initiate the
appeal of the Planning Commission’s decision, and to place the item on a future agenda.

Councilmember Savidan stated that he was in agreement with Councilmember Sanchez that
misinformation about water quality and supply is circulating in the community.

Councilmember Gazeley stated that every city in the South Bay is opposed to Senate Bill 594,
and that the City of Lomita should closely watch that bill and take the necessary steps to oppose
it, if required. Councilmember Gazeley also stated that he met with Stephen Arakawa, Manager
of the Bay-Delta Initiatives, to discuss the water supply in Southern California, as well as
potential issues related to the water supply coming from Northern California.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Savidan asked to pull Item 7.J from the Consent Agenda for further discussion.
Councilmember Traina moved to approve the Consent Agenda, minus Item 7.J. Councilmember
Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

Item 7.J: Councilmember Savidan asked for clarification on how the proposed $200,000 from
the Water Reserve Fund will be used, to which Public Works Director Damasse responded that
such it will be used to cover emergency-related contractor services, which in turn will only be
utilized in cases where existing staff cannot handle a given situation, and that any contractors
used will be paid only for the work performed. Director Damasse further stated that the
proposed funding will be used as strictly a contingency fund. Councilmember Savidan moved to
approve Item 7.J., Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading.

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Special City Council meeting held on
  August 19, 2013, and the Regular City Council meeting held on August 19, 2013.
  RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  d. Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  Page 3
   e. Monthly Report for the Community Development Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  f. Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Monthly Report for the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  h. Monthly Report regarding Economic Development Activities. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  i. June 2013 Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  j. Award of agreements to Doty Bros. Construction Company, Stephen Doreck Equipment
  Rentals, Inc., and Valverde Construction, and the allocation of $50,000 for as needed on-
  call emergency water system repair services. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  k. Approval of the purchase of two (2) electric submixers from Solar Bee/Medora Corporation
  for the Cypress Water Production Facility in the amount of $17,004. RECOMMEND
  APPROVAL.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS
8.  Discussion of the City’s Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT)

Assistant City Manager Sugano provided an overview of the staff report and added that the
current Transient Occupancy Tax of 10% is consistent with surrounding cities. According to
Assistant City Manager Sugano, for FY 2013-14, the projected revenue from the Transient
Occupancy Tax is $120,000, which in turn comes from six hotels/motels located in the City of
Lomita. Assistant City Manager Sugano concluded his presentation by stating that should City
Council decide to place a proposed increase of the tax on the ballot, it would have to be in
conjunction with the municipal election held in two years.

Councilmember Traina stated that this item was discussed about a year ago, and it was
suggested at that time to increase the Transient Occupancy Tax so that the additional funds
could be used by the LA County Sheriff’s Department to increase patrols on Pacific Coast
Highway. Furthermore, Councilmember Traina stated that Council wanted to survey existing
transient occupancy businesses in order to see whether they would be in favor of an increase in
the tax if the funds would be used by the Sheriff’s Department. Councilmember Traina also
stated that the 1% increase, as stated in the staff report as $1,300, should actually be $13,000
annually for a 1% increase and $26,000 annually for a 2% increase, respectively), as the
proposed increase is not calculated from the tax received, but rather from the gross receipts of
the transient occupancy businesses.  Councilmember Traina asked staff to verify the
calculations as presented in the staff report. Councilmember Traina also asked whether the
existing motel owners were surveyed.

Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that City Council could direct staff to conduct a survey of
the transient occupancy businesses if direction were to proceed.

James Thompson, Executive Board Member of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, stated that
the Chamber had discussed the proposed increase of the Transient Occupancy Tax at their
meeting and those in attendance were unanimously in objection to the proposed tax increase
for the following reasons: only one type of business (transient occupancy businesses) is being

  Page 4
 taxed; the proposed increase is not a great revenue generator for the City; the current Transient
Occupancy Tax is consistent with surrounding cities; and the fact that the City already has a
balanced budget, in such bad economic times, so there is no need for tax increases.

George Kivett, Member of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, concurred with the comments
and statements made by Mr. Thompson. Mr. Kivett also stated that he called all six of the
businesses that would be impacted by the proposed tax increase, and they all were concerned
about a tax increase.

Councilmember Traina moved to receive and file the report. Mayor Estrada seconded the
motion. Councilmember Traina stated that the cost of placing this measure on the ballot is
expensive, and in turn the result would not be cost effective. Furthermore, Councilmember
Traina stated that he would also like staff to survey the transient occupancy businesses, and
that he was glad that Mr. Kivett contacted the business owners prior to the meeting to gage their
interest.

Mayor Estrada rescinded her second to the previous motion. The motion died for the lack of a
second. Mayor Estrada made a substitute motion to deny the increase of the Transient
Occupancy Tax. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned in memory of Walter Oren Lindley at 8:03 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
